name: Newt Gingrich
role: US Representative from Georgia (1979–1999), Speaker of the House (1995–1999)
summary: A conservative Republican who led the 1994 Contract with America. He backed a balanced-budget amendment, term limits, welfare work requirements and deregulation, opposed gun-control bills and government-run health care, and favours a larger public role for religion and nuclear power.

abortion-legal.rationale: He voted YEA on the partial-birth abortion ban (1996 #1288, 1997 #64, 1998 #949) and on bans on federal funding of abortion (1979 #550, 1983 #170).

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He writes that immigrants "must assimilate and become American" and that the Left rejects assimilation for multiculturalism.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He voted YEA on the balanced-budget amendment in 1982 (#716), 1990 (#593), 1992 (#609), 1994 (#659) and 1995 (#47).

central-planning.rationale: He defines Big Government Socialism as a gigantically powerful government that controls or owns production, and writes that socialism "never works".

close-ties-china.rationale: He writes that "the rise of Communist China is an existential threat".

death-penalty.rationale: He voted YEA on amendments adding the death penalty for drug-related murders (1986 #783, 1988 #776).

decide-locally.rationale: He voted YEA on the Unfunded Mandate Reform Act (1995 #78), limiting federal mandates on states and localities.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He writes that those who want to abolish the Electoral College ignore the founders' lesson that pure democracy risks mob rule.

direct-votes.rationale: He cites Madison that pure democracy risks mob rule and warns against abolishing the Electoral College.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He criticizes the Davos push to cut emissions by switching to wind and solar and calls "hysteria" the climate predictions of Ehrlich and Gore; he backs innovation, nuclear and carbon capture instead.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He writes "No matter how multiethnic the country becomes, Americans must maintain a common national identity", defining the nation by shared values rather than one ethnic group.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He criticizes cutting American oil and gas production and writes that the Republican agenda omits a carbon tax or clean-energy mandate because fossil fuels are not the enemy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He writes that nuclear energy is "among the most efficient, cost competitive, and safest forms of energy" and urges investing in nuclear power.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: He voted YEA on the Canady English-proficiency amendment (1996-03-20 #944).

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He credits Edison and the continuing "tide of invention" with improvements that "affected the lives of every American", including health care and communications.

limit-guns.rationale: He voted NAY on the Brady bill (1993 #548) and the assault-weapons ban (1994 #750).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He argues that health care, energy and education perform badly because government protects them from competition, and says shareholder capitalism "requires a free market to work to mutual benefit".

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: He voted YEA to authorize US force against Iraq under UN Security Council Resolution 678 (1991-01-12 #8) and on the Bosnia deployment (1995 #839), but NAY on Haiti (1994 #1087), so the record is mixed on purposes.

military-superiority.rationale: He writes that Trump will "rebuild the US military into the world's standard" so that the armed forces are "the strongest, smartest, and most effective they have ever been".

more-religion-public.rationale: He objects to efforts to "erase religion and symbols of faith from public life", including ending school prayer and barring religious schools from public funds.

nation-first.rationale: He praises Trump for breaking "two generations of bipartisan, international, elitist efforts that submerged American interests in global interests and structures".

open-borders.rationale: He calls the Left's immigration plan a threat to sovereignty and security, says a wall "just makes sense", and asks why the rule against letting strangers into one's home does not apply to "our national home".

pollution-taxes.rationale: He says the Republican agenda will not include a carbon tax.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He writes that "Americans must maintain a common national identity" and that the Left treats America as just a place where many groups reside.

property-fundamental.rationale: He writes that people refuse to invest where politicians may take property through taxation or confiscation, and that the rule of law must guarantee the right to keep the fruits of one's work.

public-ownership.rationale: He rejects a government that "controls or owns production" and writes that socialism "never works" however bad its track record.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He praises Trump's deregulation as the largest in American history and wants power moved from Washington to states, businesses and individuals; he also says excess regulation lets corporations ignore customers.

school-vouchers.rationale: He voted YEA on the HELP Scholarships bill (1997 #563).

separate-church-state.rationale: He writes the First Amendment "is not a statement against religion" and only bars a national religion and persecution.

space-expansion.rationale: He writes that the Moon-Mars Development Project means "getting to the moon, staying on the moon, and developing it", then exploring Mars and mining the solar system, and that "we cannot afford to lose this new space race".

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He voted NAY on the Rostenkowski substitute raising the top income-tax rate (1992 #455) and YEA on the Contract With America Tax Relief Act (1995 #286).

term-limits.rationale: He voted YEA on the term-limits constitutional amendment (House roll calls 1995 #269 and 1997 #20).

total-state.rationale: He warns that "the danger of a strong government micromanaging people and censoring people represents a real threat to the concept of freedom".

traditional-family.rationale: He writes "Marriage and family are foundational in a free society" and that their breakdown threatens freedom.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He writes that government-run health care such as Medicare for All, the public option or fixing Obamacare "are ultimately dead ends".

work-for-welfare.rationale: He voted YEA on the Personal Responsibility Act (1995 #261, #859) and welfare reform (1996 #1197, #1249).

notes: Searched: economy (budget, welfare, taxes, minimum wage), liberty (guns, death penalty), society (religion, language), world (trade, Iraq, Bosnia, Haiti, China, UN), government (term limits), technology (nuclear). Most House floor speeches and the ecology, culture and globalism themes were not searched to the end; the 1990s record leaves many statements without a settled position, so they are null.
